main.title: Malala and Satyarthi win the Nobel Peace Prize
main.subtitle: Education is a right
main.summary: Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi were jointly awarded the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize for defending children’s rights and education.

cards.heading: Education is a right
cards.text: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi as joint Peace Prize laureates on 10 October 2014. Their campaigns confronted different barriers to childhood: Malala defended girls’ access to education in Pakistan, while Satyarthi worked against the exploitation of children in India. Malala had survived a Taliban attack in 2012 and continued speaking publicly for education. At seventeen, she became the youngest Nobel laureate. Sharing the award connected two campaigns across national and religious boundaries, placing the rights of children, rather than a single personality, at the centre of its message.

main.title: Interstellar
main.summary: Christopher Nolan's Interstellar appeared in 2014, following astronauts searching for a new home as crop failures and famine threaten Earth.

cards.heading: Interstellar
cards.text: Christopher Nolan's Interstellar appeared in 2014, following astronauts searching for a new home as crop failures and famine threaten Earth. Matthew McConaughey and Anne Hathaway lead the spacefaring cast. The project began with a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and physicist Kip Thorne, who later served as scientific consultant. Nolan co-wrote the screenplay with Jonathan Nolan. Filming in Canada, Iceland and Los Angeles combined large-format photography with practical models and visual effects, giving the journey physical settings while imagining environments beyond Earth.

main.title: The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies
main.subtitle: Erebor is reclaimed, and its treasure divides the victors
main.summary: The Battle of the Five Armies begins with Smaug descending on Lake-town. The people who survive then need shelter and resources, while Thorin holds Erebor and becomes increasingly possessive of its treasure. Bilbo tries to find a way through the dispute, but armies gather around the mountain and turn the reclaimed kingdom into a battlefield. Released in North America on 17 December 2014, Peter Jackson's final Hobbit film shifts the expedition's central problem from reaching a lost home to deciding what its recovery should mean for everyone around it.

cards.heading: The price of the treasure

The people who survive then need shelter and resources, while Thorin holds Erebor and becomes increasingly possessive of its treasure. Bilbo tries to find a way through the dispute, but armies gather around the mountain and turn the reclaimed kingdom into a battlefield. Released in North America on 17 December 2014, Peter Jackson's final Hobbit film shifts the expedition's central problem from reaching a lost home to deciding what its recovery should mean for everyone around it.

cards.heading: Bilbo finds his way home
cards.text: Weta Digital's work ranged from the burning town and water effects to large armies and digital landscapes around Erebor. Its Army Manager system helped organize the crowds, while the Manuka renderer supported the detailed lighting of complex scenes. Within that scale, the film follows particular confrontations and Thorin's changing relationship with Bilbo. Their farewell gives the return journey its emotional weight. Bilbo eventually reaches Bag End carrying an adventure his neighbours scarcely understand, and the ending brings this trilogy back towards the opening of The Fellowship of the Ring.

main.title: First observation of gravitational waves
main.summary: The first direct observation of gravitational waves was made on 14 September 2015 and was announced by the LIGO and Virgo collaborations on 11 February 2016.

cards.heading: First observation of gravitational waves
cards.text: The first direct observation of gravitational waves was made on 14 September 2015 and was announced by the LIGO and Virgo collaborations on 11 February 2016. Previously, gravitational waves had been inferred only indirectly, via their effect on the timing of pulsars in binary star systems. The waveform, detected by both LIGO observatories, matched the predictions of general relativity for a gravitational wave emanating from the inward spiral and merger of two black holes (of 36 M☉ and 29 M☉) and the subsequent ringdown of a single, 62 M☉ black hole remnant. The signal was named GW150914 (from gravitational wave and the date of observation 2015-09-14). It was also the first observation of a binary black hole merger, demonstrating both the existence of binary stellar-mass black hole systems and the fact that such mergers could occur within the current age of the universe.

main.title: Paris Agreement
main.summary: Negotiated by 196 parties at the 2015 UN climate conference near Paris, the Paris Agreement established shared goals for limiting global warming.

cards.heading: Paris Agreement
cards.text:
The Paris Agreement was negotiated by 196 parties at the 2015 United Nations Climate Change Conference near Paris and signed in 2016. It addresses climate-change mitigation, adaptation and finance, with a long-term goal of keeping warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and preferably limiting it to 1.5°C. These limits refer to global temperature averaged over twenty years.

By January 2026, 194 members of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change were parties to the agreement. The United States withdrew in 2020, rejoined in 2021 and withdrew again in 2026. Iran remained the major emitter among framework members that had not ratified it.

main.title: Ennio Morricone: the Oscar for The Hateful Eight
main.summary: Ennio Morricone won the Academy Award for Original Score for The Hateful Eight on 28 February 2016.

cards.heading: Ennio Morricone: the Oscar for The Hateful Eight
cards.text: Ennio Morricone won the Academy Award for Original Score for The Hateful Eight on 28 February 2016. It followed his honorary Oscar in 2007, adding a competitive award to a long career in film music. Morricone had written more than four hundred scores for cinema and television alongside classical works. His collaborations included Sergio Leone's films from A Fistful of Dollars onwards and Giuseppe Tornatore's from Cinema Paradiso. The award recognised a new score by a composer whose work had already become closely associated with several generations of cinema.

main.title: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
main.summary: AlphaGo faced Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul from 9 to 15 March 2016.

cards.heading: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
cards.text: AlphaGo faced Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul from 9 to 15 March 2016. DeepMind's program won four games in the five-game match, with Lee taking the fourth. Every game ended in resignation. The result became a prominent moment in the development of artificial intelligence, drawing comparisons with Deep Blue's 1997 chess match against Garry Kasparov. DeepMind announced that the million-dollar winner's prize would go to charities and Go organisations. The Korea Baduk Association awarded AlphaGo an honorary ninth-dan rank in recognition of its achievement.

main.title: Bob Dylan wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
main.subtitle: A song can carry literature
main.summary: On 13 October 2016 the Swedish Academy awarded Bob Dylan the Nobel Prize in Literature for his contribution to the American song tradition.

cards.heading: A song can carry literature
cards.text: The Swedish Academy named Bob Dylan the Nobel Prize in Literature laureate on October 13, 2016, recognising the new poetic expression he had created within the American song tradition. The award honoured a body of work shaped through words, voice and music. Its choice placed songwriting within a literary distinction commonly associated with novels, plays and poetry on the page, drawing attention to the literary possibilities of performed song.

main.title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
main.subtitle: Newt Scamander brings a suitcase of creatures to New York
main.summary: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them moves the wizarding world to New York in 1926. Eddie Redmayne plays Newt Scamander, a researcher whose suitcase contains creatures collected on his travels. Directed by David Yates, the film opened in Britain and the United States on 18 November 2016 and marked J.K. Rowling's screenwriting debut.

cards.heading: A new visitor to the wizarding world
cards.text: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them moves the wizarding world to New York in 1926. Eddie Redmayne plays Newt Scamander, a researcher whose suitcase contains creatures collected on his travels. Directed by David Yates, the film opened in Britain and the United States on 18 November 2016 and marked J.K. Rowling's screenwriting debut.

cards.heading: The case opens
cards.text: A case mix-up brings Newt together with Jacob Kowalski, a baker with no knowledge of magic. Creatures escape into the city, and recovering them draws both men into the lives of Tina and Queenie Goldstein. The unfamiliar streets and American magical authorities give Newt rules he does not yet understand. Jacob's encounter with the much larger world inside the suitcase lets the audience discover its habitats and inhabitants through someone who is seeing them for the first time.

cards.heading: Care instead of conquest
cards.text: Newt's work depends on noticing how each creature behaves and what it needs. That gives the chases and encounters different rhythms: a small animal attracted to valuables demands another response from a frightened or powerful creature. The film's wider danger develops alongside these acts of care, bringing concealment and persecution into the same city. James Newton Howard's score supplies a new musical identity, while the production reunites Yates with Harry Potter collaborators including designer Stuart Craig and producer David Heyman.

main.title: MeToo movement
main.summary: The #MeToo hashtag spread widely in October 2017 after reports of sexual-abuse allegations against producer Harvey Weinstein.

cards.heading: MeToo movement
cards.text: The #MeToo hashtag spread widely in October 2017 after reports of sexual-abuse allegations against producer Harvey Weinstein. Survivors shared experiences of harassment and assault, making their prevalence publicly visible. Activist Tarana Burke had used the phrase in this context around 2006, grounding it in empathy and solidarity. On 15 October 2017, actress Alyssa Milano encouraged women to post the words on social media. The resulting wave of testimony brought individual accounts into a collective discussion, with workplace abuse and the power enabling it becoming central public concerns.
